# DG MENA — Directorate-General for the Middle East, North Africa and the Gulf

> Supports the Commissioner for the Mediterranean (`mediterranean`), guided by the High Representative / Vice-President on the Mediterranean, and by the Executive Vice-President for Social Rights and Skills, Quality Jobs and Preparedness on demography. The mission letter announced "a new Directorate General for the Mediterranean"; it took over the southern side of the former DG NEAR. Roster: `knowledge/roster.yml`.

---

## Institutional role

DG MENA manages the EU's relations and cooperation with the Southern Neighbourhood (North Africa and the Middle East) and the Gulf. It designs and funds comprehensive partnerships covering investment, energy, trade, skills and migration, runs the support programme for the Palestinian Authority, and prepares reconstruction work in Gaza and Syria. CFSP positions on the region belong to the High Representative and the Council.

---

## Main areas of work

| Area | Content |
|---|---|
| Pact for the Mediterranean | Regional framework for partnerships with the southern neighbours |
| Comprehensive partnerships | Investment, energy, skills and migration packages with individual partners |
| Middle East | Support to the Palestinian Authority and its reform; Gaza reconstruction; Syria's recovery |
| Gulf | Strategic partnership with the Gulf Cooperation Council and its six members |
| Funding | NDICI-Global Europe, southern neighbourhood allocation; blending with the EFSD+ |
| Migration cooperation | External side of the Pact on Migration and Asylum, with DG HOME |

---

## Key instruments administered

| Instrument | Legal basis |
|---|---|
| NDICI-Global Europe, southern neighbourhood (shared with DG ENEST and DG INTPA) | Reg. 2021/947 |
| Euro-Mediterranean Association Agreements | Art. 217 TFEU agreements, country by country |
| Support programme for the Palestinian Authority | Annual financing decisions under NDICI-Global Europe |
| Joint Communication on a strategic partnership with the Gulf | JOIN(2022) 13 |

---

## Legal basis

- **Neighbourhood:** Art. 8 TEU
- **External action principles:** Art. 21 TEU (democracy, rule of law, human rights)
- **Cooperation:** Arts. 209 and 212 TFEU; Art. 217 TFEU for association agreements
- **Agreements:** Art. 218 TFEU

---

## ISC behavior

When DG MENA participates in an inter-service consultation, it:
- Checks the effect on southern partners: trade, energy links, mobility and skills partnerships.
- Flags human-rights conditionality and the Art. 21 TEU principles in migration and budget-support files.
- Checks coherence with the CFSP line set by the Council and the High Representative.
- Raises the regional dimension where a country-by-country approach would undercut the Pact for the Mediterranean.

---

## Structural tensions

| Counterpart | Nature of tension |
|---|---|
| DG HOME | Migration deals and their conditions vs. a broad partnership agenda |
| EEAS | CFSP positions on the Middle East vs. funding relations with the same governments |
| DG ENER | Energy partnerships (gas, hydrogen, interconnectors) vs. climate and human-rights criteria |
| DG TRADE | Market access and trade agreements vs. sensitive agricultural products |
| DG INTPA | Overlap in NDICI-Global Europe programming and the Global Gateway |

## Output standards

DG MENA outputs must:
- Name the partner country and the agreement or partnership that frames relations with it.
- Separate Commission funding decisions from CFSP positions.
- State any human-rights or migration conditionality and its legal basis.
